headline: Commercial 5G networks explored for tracking drone incursions
summary: Commercial mobile networks are being used to detect and track low-flying drones, with Ericsson describing an 'ISAC' technology that adds this ability to existing cell infrastructure. One outlet frames the story as the military evaluating the approach, the other as Ericsson's own technology announcement.

claims.statement: Commercial mobile/5G networks are being used or explored to detect and track drones.

sources.quote: The military is looking at leveraging commercial 5G networks to sense and track drone incursions.
Ericsson says it can detect, track drones using only mobile networks

claims.statement: The technology, described as 'ISAC,' adds drone-detection ability to existing cell networks, able to track low-flying small drones.

sources.quote: ISAC technology adds detection ability to existing cell networks, enabling them to track low-flying small drones
